analysis.summary: The provided Python code contains multiple security and quality issues, including hardcoded credentials, SQL injection, broken cryptography, command injection, and logging sensitive data. Additionally, the code violates several best practices and standards.

security_issues.title: Use of Hardcoded Credentials
security_issues.description: The code contains hardcoded AWS access key and secret, which can be easily extracted and misused.
security_issues.remediation: Remove hardcoded credentials and use environment variables or a secure vault.

security_issues.title: Use of Weak Cryptographic Algorithm
security_issues.description: The code uses MD5 for signature verification, which is considered weak and vulnerable to collision attacks.
security_issues.remediation: Use a stronger cryptographic algorithm like SHA-256 for signature verification.
security_issues.fixed_snippet:
import hashlib
signature = hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()
if signature == "expected_hash":
    return True

security_issues.title: SQL Injection
security_issues.description: The code constructs SQL queries by concatenating strings, which can lead to SQL injection attacks.
security_issues.remediation: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.

security_issues.title: Logging Sensitive Data
security_issues.description: The code logs user payloads, which may contain sensitive information such as PII or credit card details.
security_issues.remediation: Sanitize or remove sensitive data before logging.

security_issues.title: Command Injection
security_issues.description: The code passes user input directly to a shell command, which can lead to command injection attacks.
security_issues.remediation: Avoid using shell=True and validate or sanitize user input before executing commands.

quality_issues.title: Global Variables
quality_issues.description: The code uses global variables for configuration, which can lead to maintainability issues.
quality_issues.remediation: Use configuration files or environment variables for global settings.

quality_issues.title: Magic Numbers
quality_issues.description: The code uses magic numbers for configuration, which can lead to maintainability issues.
quality_issues.remediation: Use named constants or configuration files for magic numbers.

quality_issues.title: Too Many Arguments
quality_issues.description: The OrderProcessorModule classes have too many arguments in their constructors, which can lead to maintainability issues.
quality_issues.snippet: def __init__(self, data, context, user, flags, config, db_conn, logger, cache):
quality_issues.remediation: Refactor the constructor to use a single configuration object or reduce the number of arguments.

quality_issues.title: Cognitive Complexity
quality_issues.description: The legacy_calculation_C methods have high cognitive complexity, which can lead to maintainability issues.
quality_issues.remediation: Refactor the method to reduce complexity and improve readability.
quality_issues.fixed_snippet:

quality_issues.title: Redundant Code
quality_issues.description: The log_event_shard functions are redundant and can be refactored into a single function.
quality_issues.remediation: Refactor the functions into a single function with a parameter for the shard number.

business_logic_issues.description: The OrderProcessorModule classes have identical logic, which can be refactored into a single class with a parameter for the module ID.
